**Original Question:**
List the nationalities of each of the drivers which scored over one point in both the 1986 and 1988 French Formula 1 Grand Prix.

**Previous Reasoning Steps:**
[turn 1] We need nationalities of drivers who scored over one point in both the 1986 and 1988 French GP.

We need results for French GP 1986 and 1988. In F1, points were awarded to top 6 (9-6-4-3-2-1). "Over one point" means >1 point, so at least 2 points (so positions 1-5). Must have scored at least 2 points in both races.

Hence list drivers who finished in positions 1-5 in 1986 and also positions 1-5 in 1988.

Let's recall: 1986 French GP: This was the first race after the new points? Actually 1986 points: 9-6-4-3-2-1. 1986 French GP (La Prairie?) Let's quickly search.

[turn 2] We need drivers scoring over one point in both 1986 and 1988 French GP. In F1 1986 points: winner gets 9? Actually 1986: points for 1st 9, 2nd 6, 3rd 4, 4th 3, 5th 2, 6th 1. So over one point is >=2 points. So drivers finishing 1-5 in both races. Need the nationalities of each driver.

We need 1988 French GP as well. Search.

[turn 3] The user asks: "List the nationalities of each of the drivers which scored over one point in both the 1986 and 1988 French Formula 1 Grand Prix." We need to interpret.

In Formula 1, drivers get points according to finishing positions. Historically, scoring over one point means finishing positions that awarded more than 1 point.

We need to find drivers who scored more than 1 point in both 1986 and 1988 French GP. Then list their nationalities.

Which positions awarded points in those years? The points system changed over time. In 1986 and 1988, the points system was 9-6-4-3-2-1 for finishing 1st to 6th. The 5/3/2/1 was later. So points are awarded to the first 6.

Thus drivers finishing in positions 1-6 have at least 1 point, but only 6th gets 1 point. They said scored over one point: thus finishing first through fifth (since 6th is only 1). But the text says "over one point" meaning strictly >1 point, so they need to have at least 2 points. So 6th not included.

Thus we need drivers who finished 1-5 in both races.

Let's find the results for both races.

Motor car race

The **1986 French Grand Prix** was a [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One")[motor race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_race "Motor race") held at [Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard") on 6 July 1986. It was the eighth race of the [1986 Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship "1986 Formula One World Championship").

Following [Elio de Angelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis")'s fatal testing crash on the full 5.81-kilometre (3.61 mi) circuit two months previously, a decision was made to use the shorter, 3.812-kilometre (2.369 mi) "Club" circuit for this race and for future F1 races (up to and including [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_French_Grand_Prix "1990 French Grand Prix")). This eliminated the high-speed Verrerie bends, where de Angelis had crashed, and reduced the length of the Mistral straight from 1.8 km (1.1 mi) to 1 km (0.62 mi). Nonetheless, the cars still recorded speeds of over 330 km/h (205 mph) on the straight.

The 80-lap race was won by [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell"), driving a [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_FW11 "Williams FW11")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"). It was Mansell's third victory of the season. [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") finished second in a [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MP4/2 "McLaren MP4/2")-[TAG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techniques_d'Avant_Garde "Techniques d'Avant Garde"), with [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") third in the other Williams-Honda. [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") took [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position") in his [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_98T "Lotus 98T")-[Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One"), but crashed at Signes early in the race after sliding on oil laid by [Andrea de Cesaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_de_Cesaris "Andrea de Cesaris")'s failed [Minardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minardi "Minardi").

This race marked [Scuderia Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari")'s 400th start in a World Championship event as a team.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-2)

Motor car race

The **1986 French Grand Prix** was a [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One")[motor race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_race "Motor race") held at [Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard") on 6 July 1986. It was the eighth race of the [1986 Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship "1986 Formula One World Championship").

Following [Elio de Angelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis")'s fatal testing crash on the full 5.81-kilometre (3.61 mi) circuit two months previously, a decision was made to use the shorter, 3.812-kilometre (2.369 mi) "Club" circuit for this race and for future F1 races (up to and including [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_French_Grand_Prix "1990 French Grand Prix")). This eliminated the high-speed Verrerie bends, where de Angelis had crashed, and reduced the length of the Mistral straight from 1.8 km (1.1 mi) to 1 km (0.62 mi). Nonetheless, the cars still recorded speeds of over 330 km/h (205 mph) on the straight.

The 80-lap race was won by [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell"), driving a [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_FW11 "Williams FW11")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"). It was Mansell's third victory of the season. [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") finished second in a [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MP4/2 "McLaren MP4/2")-[TAG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techniques_d'Avant_Garde "Techniques d'Avant Garde"), with [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") third in the other Williams-Honda. [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") took [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position") in his [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_98T "Lotus 98T")-[Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One"), but crashed at Signes early in the race after sliding on oil laid by [Andrea de Cesaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_de_Cesaris "Andrea de Cesaris")'s failed [Minardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minardi "Minardi").

This race marked [Scuderia Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari")'s 400th start in a World Championship event as a team.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-2)

Motor car race

The **1988 French Grand Prix** was a [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") motor race held on 3 July 1988 at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard"), [Le Castellet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Castellet,_Var "Le Castellet, Var"). It was the seventh race of the [1988 Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Formula_One_World_Championship "1988 Formula One World Championship").

The 80-lap race was won by local driver [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"), driving a [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"), after he started from [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position"). Prost's Brazilian teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") finished second, with Italian [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") third in a [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari").

## Qualifying

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Qualifying")]

The two [McLarens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MP4/4 "McLaren MP4/4") lined up in their usual front row places, but, for the first time this season, [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") was ahead of [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna"), the Frenchman beating the Brazilian by almost half a second to take his first pole since the [1986 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1986 Monaco Grand Prix") and in doing so stopping his teammate from a record-breaking 7th pole in succession. The two [Ferraris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_F1/87#F1/87/88C "Ferrari F1/87") filled the second row, [Gerhard Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger") beating [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") by over 1.1 seconds, though neither driver believed they could race with the McLarens simply because of fuel consumption. On the third row were the two [normally-aspirated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturally_aspirated_engine "Naturally aspirated engine")[Benettons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_B188 "Benetton B188") of [Thierry Boutsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Boutsen "Thierry Boutsen") and [Alessandro Nannini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nannini "Alessandro Nannini"), while the [Lotuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_100T "Lotus 100T") of [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") and [Satoru Nakajima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoru_Nakajima "Satoru Nakajima") filled the fourth row, Piquet being the last driver to qualify under 1:10. The top ten was completed by the [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_FW12 "Williams FW12") of [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") (over 2.7 seconds slower than Prost and almost 4 seconds slower than his [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") pole time) and the [March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_881 "March 881") of [Ivan Capelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Capelli "Ivan Capelli"), who had recovered after fracturing his left foot in a crash during practice in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Detroit_Grand_Prix "1988 Detroit Grand Prix") two weeks before.

Meanwhile, [Ligier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier") had a disastrous weekend on their home turf with both [René Arnoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Arnoux "René Arnoux"), a winner with [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") at the circuit in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_French_Grand_Prix "1982 French Grand Prix"), and [Stefan Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Johansson "Stefan Johansson") failing to qualify, though they did have a celebration of sorts over the weekend as Arnoux turned 40 the day after the race. [Julian Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Bailey_(racing_driver) "Julian Bailey (racing driver)") also failed to qualify in his [Tyrrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrrell_017 "Tyrrell 017"), while [Piercarlo Ghinzani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piercarlo_Ghinzani "Piercarlo Ghinzani") qualified 22nd in his [Zakspeed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakspeed_881 "Zakspeed 881") but was excluded for missing a weight check, thus promoting [Oscar Larrauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Larrauri "Oscar Larrauri")'s [EuroBrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroBrun_ER188 "EuroBrun ER188") to the last grid spot.

## Race summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Race summary")]

Prost led away from Senna and the two Ferraris, with Piquet passing the two Benettons for fifth. Despite worries in the McLaren pit about overly high fuel consumption (the fuel readouts in the cars were showing less fuel used than what the Honda telemetry was telling the team), Ron Dennis was reportedly prepared to let his drivers run out of fuel at the expense of a perfect season if it taught them to be more conservative given their obvious advantage over the field, though ultimately the onboard readouts were proved correct. Prost maintained a two-second advantage over Senna until the mid-race pit stops, while an early stop by Berger on lap 22 allowed teammate Alboreto through into third. While both McLarens were racing each other out front, they were still pulling away from the field at sometimes a second per lap.

Senna made his pit stop three laps before Prost, enabling him to take the lead thanks to a slow stop for Prost with a sticking front wheel, but traffic on the Mistral Straight (including a less than helpful Piquet who most likely enjoyed seeing Senna lose the lead to Prost at close quarters) and a gearbox problem allowed Prost to close right up to him and then overtake him on lap 61 as they lapped [Alex Caffi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Caffi "Alex Caffi") and [Pierluigi Martini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierluigi_Martini "Pierluigi Martini") at the Signes corner. Meanwhile, Berger reclaimed third only for Alboreto to pass him again during the pit stops, while Mansell suffered his seventh consecutive retirement, dropping out on lap 49 with suspension problems, though he had been dropping back for a number of laps with power loss from his [Judd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_(engine)#CV "Judd (engine)")[V8 engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_engine "V8 engine"). After returning to the pits and getting himself cleaned up, the Englishman left the circuit profoundly fed up with the performance of the Williams, fuelling ongoing speculation in the press that he would leave the team at the end of the year to join Ferrari after the Italian team had announced they would not be keeping Alboreto for 1989. Despite the rumours turning out to be correct, Mansell continued to deny he was joining Ferrari.

In the closing laps, Prost pulled away as Senna's gearbox troubles continued, losing several gears. The Brazilian eventually finished nearly 32 seconds behind the Frenchman, though he was still nearly 35 seconds ahead of Alboreto, the last man on the lead lap. Berger was fourth ahead of Piquet, who also suffered gearbox problems in the later stages of the race; the final point went to the Benetton of Nannini. France was the first time since the [1987 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1987 Monaco Grand Prix") that Alboreto had finished in front of his teammate in a race where they both finished. During the race Alboreto had the advantage of an almost perfectly balanced car, while Berger complained of severe understeer, something not needed at the high speed Signes corner at the end of the Mistral.

The fastest lap of the race, a 1:11.737 set by Prost on lap 45, was over two seconds slower than the 1:09.548 set by Piquet in a Honda-powered Williams the [previous year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") – a consequence of the restrictions imposed on [turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines this season with the major difference being the speeds attained on the now 1 km long Mistral Straight. In 1987 the fastest turbo cars (Honda powered) were timed at 325 km/h (202 mph) on the straight. In 1988 the top speed was recorded at 311 km/h (193 mph).

For Prost it was his third win in his home Grand Prix after winning in both [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_French_Grand_Prix "1981 French Grand Prix") at [Dijon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dijon-Prenois "Dijon-Prenois") (his first Grand Prix victory) and [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_French_Grand_Prix "1983 French Grand Prix") at the full length Paul Ricard. On both occasions he had been driving for the factory [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Renault "Equipe Renault") team.

Motor car race

The **1988 French Grand Prix** was a [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") motor race held on 3 July 1988 at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard"), [Le Castellet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Castellet,_Var "Le Castellet, Var"). It was the seventh race of the [1988 Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Formula_One_World_Championship "1988 Formula One World Championship").

The 80-lap race was won by local driver [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"), driving a [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"), after he started from [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position"). Prost's Brazilian teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") finished second, with Italian [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") third in a [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari").

## Qualifying

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Qualifying")]

The two [McLarens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MP4/4 "McLaren MP4/4") lined up in their usual front row places, but, for the first time this season, [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") was ahead of [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna"), the Frenchman beating the Brazilian by almost half a second to take his first pole since the [1986 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1986 Monaco Grand Prix") and in doing so stopping his teammate from a record-breaking 7th pole in succession. The two [Ferraris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_F1/87#F1/87/88C "Ferrari F1/87") filled the second row, [Gerhard Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger") beating [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") by over 1.1 seconds, though neither driver believed they could race with the McLarens simply because of fuel consumption. On the third row were the two [normally-aspirated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturally_aspirated_engine "Naturally aspirated engine")[Benettons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_B188 "Benetton B188") of [Thierry Boutsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Boutsen "Thierry Boutsen") and [Alessandro Nannini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nannini "Alessandro Nannini"), while the [Lotuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_100T "Lotus 100T") of [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") and [Satoru Nakajima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoru_Nakajima "Satoru Nakajima") filled the fourth row, Piquet being the last driver to qualify under 1:10. The top ten was completed by the [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_FW12 "Williams FW12") of [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") (over 2.7 seconds slower than Prost and almost 4 seconds slower than his [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") pole time) and the [March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_881 "March 881") of [Ivan Capelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Capelli "Ivan Capelli"), who had recovered after fracturing his left foot in a crash during practice in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Detroit_Grand_Prix "1988 Detroit Grand Prix") two weeks before.

Meanwhile, [Ligier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier") had a disastrous weekend on their home turf with both [René Arnoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Arnoux "René Arnoux"), a winner with [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") at the circuit in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_French_Grand_Prix "1982 French Grand Prix"), and [Stefan Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Johansson "Stefan Johansson") failing to qualify, though they did have a celebration of sorts over the weekend as Arnoux turned 40 the day after the race. [Julian Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Bailey_(racing_driver) "Julian Bailey (racing driver)") also failed to qualify in his [Tyrrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrrell_017 "Tyrrell 017"), while [Piercarlo Ghinzani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piercarlo_Ghinzani "Piercarlo Ghinzani") qualified 22nd in his [Zakspeed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakspeed_881 "Zakspeed 881") but was excluded for missing a weight check, thus promoting [Oscar Larrauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Larrauri "Oscar Larrauri")'s [EuroBrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroBrun_ER188 "EuroBrun ER188") to the last grid spot.

## Race summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Race summary")]

Prost led away from Senna and the two Ferraris, with Piquet passing the two Benettons for fifth. Despite worries in the McLaren pit about overly high fuel consumption (the fuel readouts in the cars were showing less fuel used than what the Honda telemetry was telling the team), Ron Dennis was reportedly prepared to let his drivers run out of fuel at the expense of a perfect season if it taught them to be more conservative given their obvious advantage over the field, though ultimately the onboard readouts were proved correct. Prost maintained a two-second advantage over Senna until the mid-race pit stops, while an early stop by Berger on lap 22 allowed teammate Alboreto through into third. While both McLarens were racing each other out front, they were still pulling away from the field at sometimes a second per lap.

Senna made his pit stop three laps before Prost, enabling him to take the lead thanks to a slow stop for Prost with a sticking front wheel, but traffic on the Mistral Straight (including a less than helpful Piquet who most likely enjoyed seeing Senna lose the lead to Prost at close quarters) and a gearbox problem allowed Prost to close right up to him and then overtake him on lap 61 as they lapped [Alex Caffi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Caffi "Alex Caffi") and [Pierluigi Martini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierluigi_Martini "Pierluigi Martini") at the Signes corner. Meanwhile, Berger reclaimed third only for Alboreto to pass him again during the pit stops, while Mansell suffered his seventh consecutive retirement, dropping out on lap 49 with suspension problems, though he had been dropping back for a number of laps with power loss from his [Judd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_(engine)#CV "Judd (engine)")[V8 engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_engine "V8 engine"). After returning to the pits and getting himself cleaned up, the Englishman left the circuit profoundly fed up with the performance of the Williams, fuelling ongoing speculation in the press that he would leave the team at the end of the year to join Ferrari after the Italian team had announced they would not be keeping Alboreto for 1989. Despite the rumours turning out to be correct, Mansell continued to deny he was joining Ferrari.

In the closing laps, Prost pulled away as Senna's gearbox troubles continued, losing several gears. The Brazilian eventually finished nearly 32 seconds behind the Frenchman, though he was still nearly 35 seconds ahead of Alboreto, the last man on the lead lap. Berger was fourth ahead of Piquet, who also suffered gearbox problems in the later stages of the race; the final point went to the Benetton of Nannini. France was the first time since the [1987 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1987 Monaco Grand Prix") that Alboreto had finished in front of his teammate in a race where they both finished. During the race Alboreto had the advantage of an almost perfectly balanced car, while Berger complained of severe understeer, something not needed at the high speed Signes corner at the end of the Mistral.

The fastest lap of the race, a 1:11.737 set by Prost on lap 45, was over two seconds slower than the 1:09.548 set by Piquet in a Honda-powered Williams the [previous year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") – a consequence of the restrictions imposed on [turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines this season with the major difference being the speeds attained on the now 1 km long Mistral Straight. In 1987 the fastest turbo cars (Honda powered) were timed at 325 km/h (202 mph) on the straight. In 1988 the top speed was recorded at 311 km/h (193 mph).

For Prost it was his third win in his home Grand Prix after winning in both [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_French_Grand_Prix "1981 French Grand Prix") at [Dijon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dijon-Prenois "Dijon-Prenois") (his first Grand Prix victory) and [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_French_Grand_Prix "1983 French Grand Prix") at the full length Paul Ricard. On both occasions he had been driving for the factory [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Renault "Equipe Renault") team.
